summary: A socket server cannot write its own memory document: registerMemory gives no write, and takes one only from a createLocal() caller
detail: The rule (kinds.md): a memory document is written by a caller in this process, the server that knows who is connected; over a socket a delta is 403. The trap: registered on createWs(), the server has no such caller. registerMemory returns peek and forget only, and its delta handler takes a write only from a client with data.local, which only createLocal() makes. examples/lobby registers it on a tee ({ ...ws, on: (a, h) => (ws.on(a, h), local.server.on(a, h)) }) and writes with local.call("delta", ...); kinds.md teaches the tee. The change that removes it: registerMemory returns write(name, ops) (applied, versioned and told as a local delta is, answering its error codes); kinds.md and the lobby then write with it, and the tee goes.
note: 2026-10-20: opened by root #116 (examples/lobby); 2026-10-20: fixed: registerMemory returns write(name, ops), applied, versioned and told as a local delta is, answering { result: { ack, version, ops } } or { error } (404, 400, and 400 for a name not of the prefix); the lobby writes with it and its tee is gone, kinds.md teaches it (tests/kinds.test.ts, "a socket server writes its own"). registerSource and registerStatic need none: a source pushes through subscribe, a static changes with a release

summary: connectWs sends no cookie outside a browser, so a script or test signed in by link cannot use openDoc
detail: The rule (auth.md): the socket is signed in by the session cookie on the upgrade, never a token in the URL. The trap: Bun's WebSocket takes headers, but connectWs (reconnectingWebSocket) opens new WebSocket(url) with none, so a Bun client of an auth-link app is nobody. delta's tests speak the wire by hand on Bun's own WebSocket (signedIn in tests/helpers/examples.ts), and the browser helper swaps globalThis.WebSocket for one that adds the cookie; auth.md says so as a gotcha. The change that removes it: ConnectOptions.headers (or cookie), passed on each connect where the runtime takes them (Bun), ignored in a browser; then a script uses connectWs and openDoc as a page does, and the gotcha goes.
note: 2026-10-20: opened by root #116 (examples/lists); 2026-10-20: fixed: ConnectOptions.headers (chosen over a cookie option: an authorization rides the same way), sent on every connect where the runtime takes them (Bun), ignored in a browser. signedIn in tests/helpers/examples.ts is connectWs with the cookie, and the lists tests use openDoc, call, undo and history; the lists browser helper no longer swaps globalThis.WebSocket (happy-dom's own sends the cookie from its jar); auth.md's gotcha is gone (tests/client.test.ts, "connectWs headers")

summary: A session that runs out drops every subscription of its socket, an ANYONE document's too
detail: linkAuth's gate, finding a session run out, deletes the identity and calls dropClientSubscriptions: right for every document it was signed in for, but the socket also stops hearing an `owns: "ANYONE"` document it may still have, though it is not told so and a fresh open would admit it. Every backend's letGo already releases the others at the next change (401), so the drop could keep the ANYONE documents' subscriptions; the gate does not know the documents. For Peter: whether a socket whose session runs out keeps hearing what anyone may.
note: 2026-10-21: found while making `owns: "ANYONE"` (the Shed's run 6, finding 5): left as it is, since the client reconnects on the 401 it is told and opens the document again. Not fixed 2026-10-21: the client already reconnects on its 401 and opens the document again, so a run-out session loses a reconnect, nothing it may hear; keeping the subscriptions would make the gate know the documents. When a story needs no gap at all: the gate asks each subscription's owns rather than dropping them all.

summary: An ANYONE document with no accept is written by anyone, signed in or not
detail: `owns: "ANYONE"` opens a document to a socket nobody is signed in on, and its writes are the document's rule (`accept`, told `who` undefined), as decided. Without an `accept` every socket writes it, the hole the Shed's run 6 found (finding 3: a visitor rewrote the list). registerDocs could refuse an ANYONE document with no accept, as it refuses one with no owns (default-deny for writing). For Peter.
note: 2026-10-21: left open: ownership.md says to give such a document its rule, and the cases give board: one. Fixed 2026-10-21: defineDoc refuses an ANYONE document with no accept (default-deny for writing, as for opening); ownership.md says so.

summary: A client-named id near 2^53-1 may leave a SQLite table unable to mint, as dzql #82 did on Postgres
detail: dzql bounds its serial below 2^53-1 (less 2^32) so add /<coll>/- always mints an id a path names; SQLite's serial (write.ts) and importTables (carry.ts, which sets sequences past imported ids) have no such bound. Check with the same probe (add /courses/9007199254740991, then add /courses/-, then remove it) on SQLite and the JSON file; a fix belongs in a shared case. (Found fixing dzql #82, 22 October.)

summary: noOverlap counts every current row: a declined request still holds its days
detail: leave's requests: a person cannot ask again for days a request of theirs was declined over, since the declined row is current. unique has a where/whereNull; noOverlap may want the same (count only the rows where status is not declined). (Found building #100, 22 October.)
